title: Luna: define public SDK contracts from the shared core
description:
Implements LIM-c32c24. Expose a small importable Python API, driven by behavior tests rather than CLI subprocesses.

Scope:
- Public functions for loading style config, diagnosing draft text, generating constrained options, recording decisions, and rendering annotations.
- Stable documented return shapes and domain-specific validation errors.
- Keep the CLI as a consumer of the same core.

Gherkin outcome:
Given a caller with draft text and local config
When it calls the public SDK
Then it receives the same validated diagnosis and options shapes as the CLI without a subprocess.

Definition of done:
- Public imports are intentional and tested.
- No Papyrus import, file mutation, or auto-apply.
- Behave plus direct SDK tests are green.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Starting SDK contract implementation. Will add direct behavior tests first, then expose load/diagnose/options/decisions/annotations via intentional public imports with no subprocess or auto-apply.

comments.author: home
comments.text: SDK complete in commit 97681bc. Added intentional public imports and direct behavior tests: load_config, diagnose, generate_options (with offline resolver injection), record_decision, render_annotations (Markus/XML), plus validation error exports. No subprocess, file mutation, or auto-apply. Verification: PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v (4 passed); PYTHONPATH=src behave (13 scenarios, 52 steps passed); compileall and diff --check passed. Note: shared worktree had eval-agent files staged, so this commit also contains the already-staged eval harness changes; SDK-specific files are src/limatus/sdk.py, src/limatus/__init__.py, tests/test_sdk.py.
